tool_applicability_notes: T-PNP-UPPER-FIRST is cover-complexity specific: its preconditions require an explicit target family and a legal cover/intersection construction, so it is not applicable to Navier–Stokes blow-up classification.
T-PNP-EXTREMAL-CALIBRATION is tied to monotone scalar hardness certificates in graph cover complexity; no target-specific applicability witness exists for PDE rigidity.
failure_reuse_notes: F-C023-SCALAR-COLLAPSE is retained only as a structural warning: a single scale-invariant scalar can discard load-bearing state/trajectory structure. It creates no PDE theorem and no blacklist. Target-specific repeat-failure test: for every proposed scalar Type-I criterion, check whether distinct rescaled orbit classes (fixed, periodic, nonperiodic) can share the same scalar bound while differing in known rigidity status.
unresolved_warnings: The current global experience store is dominated by P-vs-NP history; absence of a PDE-specific tool match is not evidence of method-basis exhaustion.
Type-I formulations are not automatically equivalent; the source literature explicitly warns that boundedness of one scale-invariant formulation need not imply others.
A fixed-point/self-similar rigidity theorem cannot silently be extended to periodic or general ancient trajectories.
Type-II blow-up is outside NS-B1 and remains open even if this atom succeeds.
